friends in activities are related to academic outcomes, and this association is mediated by school belonging.
friends in extracurrucular activities were related to academic outcomes, and that the link between friends and academics was mediated by school belonging.

friends in extracuriousricular activities are linked to academic outcomes, in part through school belonging, and that this link replicates across ethnicity and the type and level of activity involvement.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how youth's peer relationships in school-related activities affect their academic outcomes.
how the peer relations in extracurriculum activities are linked to academic outcomes.
the role of friends in activities in the academic lives of adolescents in middle school.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
friends in activities, school belonging, and academic outcomes are related to each other in a way that is not influenced by the type of activity or by ethnicity.

the results of this study are consistent with the idea that students who are involved in activities with friends who are also involved in activities are more likely to have positive feelings toward the school and are more likely to do well in school.
friends in activities, particularly friends who share a similar ethnic identity, are important for school belonging, and that this is linked to better academic outcomes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

students who are involved in extracuricular activities with friends are more likely to have a sense of belonging at school, and that this sense of school belonging is associated with higher academic achievement and engagement.
friends in activities are important for students' academic engagement and achievement and that this is particularly true for students who have fewer friends in general.
friends in activities can be a source of positive influence, particularly when they are also sources of social and emotional support and a sense of belonging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the benefits of participating in extracurriculum activities for academic outcomes are not limited to those who have friends within activities.
the quality of peer relations in school-based activities may matter for academic outcomes, and this is particularly important for students in diverse middle schools.
the social environment of school-based activities is an important context in which to consider how peer relations can promote academic success.
